- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.17) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.0) and price is trending down, avoid sharp downward corrections — instead, allow a slight lagged mean reversion to prevent premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model should undercorrect for 2–3 days to reflect market cooling, not immediate reversal.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.17), model should smooth out extreme forecast swings — especially if recent history shows mean reversion toward 65–75 range.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 5–10% gap), reduce next-day forecast by 2–3% to account for downward bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment spikes, model should anticipate a 1–2 day lagged correction — don’t assume immediate reversal.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 18-day average unless sentiment is strongly negative — this prevents underestimating downside risk.
